facts.x86_to_arm_notes: Only the RVA changes. The host function win32_d3d_compile keeps the identical 11-argument prototype (GameD3DCompileFn); on ARM the compiler spills args 5..11 to the stack in the same order the game does, so no asm is needed. The runtime content of the cell is the export address of D3DCOMPILER_47!D3DCompile WITH the Thumb bit set; save it unchanged in original_d3d_compile and store &win32_d3d_compile (the compiler sets bit0 for Thumb functions automatically). On disk the cell holds the unbound name RVA (0x01328416), so do not use the on-disk value as an expected-bytes check. The cell lives in .rdata (0xC37000..0xC37BF8): VirtualProtect(PAGE_READWRITE) it exactly like x86. The thunk at 0x00A3B944 is movw ip,#0x70B4; movt ip,#0x103; ldr.w pc,[ip] (VA 0x010370B4 = RVA 0x00C370B4), so patching the cell redirects every caller.

Callers: 0x005BD3D0 (3 calls: stages at this+4/+8/+0xC) and 0x004A1DF0. Flow: (1) build macro list; (2) D3DPreprocess(src, includes) -> text -> hash -> shader-cache lookup (D3DPreprocess output is only a cache key); (3) on cache miss D3DCompile(original source, same macros, same HeaderInclude); (4) on failure logs 'HLSL Compiler error: ' + errors; on success copies bytecode into this+0x40 and writes the cache file; (5) stage type this+0x30 (0 vs, 1 ps, 2 gs) later selects CreateVertex/Pixel/GeometryShader.

facts.summary: game's ID3DInclude implementation HeaderInclude: vtable 0x0136B164 = {Open = 0x005BB180, Close = 0x0008B980 (ICF'd 12-byte stub 'movs r0,#0; return', shared with AbsorptionMobEffect::vf4)}. Layout identical to ID3DInclude (no IUnknown): slot0 Open, slot1 Close.
facts.arm_signature: HRESULT Open(HeaderInclude* this /*r0*/, D3D_INCLUDE_TYPE type /*r1, unused*/, const char* fileName /*r2*/, const void* parentData /*r3, unused*/, const void** ppData /*[sp+0]*/, UINT* pBytes /*[sp+4]*/) -> 0 (S_OK); HRESULT Close(this /*r0*/, const void* data /*r1*/) -> 0
facts.x86_to_arm_notes: The x86 proxy (win32_include_proxy_open/close) is source-compatible: it calls original->lpVtbl->Open/Close with the standard 6/2-argument ID3DInclude prototypes, which the ARM compiler maps to AAPCS (ppData and pBytes on the stack) exactly like the game's callee reads them. HeaderInclude::Open ignores type and parentData, reads the file through the game's own resource provider registry, returns *ppData = pointer into a std::string whose heap buffer is moved into a vector inside the HeaderInclude object (valid until the HeaderInclude is destroyed after D3DCompile returns), *pBytes = size without terminating NUL. Close is a no-op returning 0. Nothing in the proxy depends on game struct offsets. The proxy is only useful if text patching of include files is kept (see gfx_compat.hlsl_lod_patch).

facts.x86_symbol: install_scissor_fix / win32_set_scissor_rects: patches ID3D11DeviceContext vtable slot 45 (RSSetScissorRects) of game_context = *(renderer+0x110)
facts.summary: The hook itself is a data patch of d3d11.dll's own vtable and is architecture independent (slot 45, 4-byte slots on ARM32 too): keep it unchanged. The game's single RSSetScissorRects call site is gfx:Renderer::setScissorRect (0x005BB560): it converts four normalized floats (s0..s3 = x, y, w, h in 0..1, bottom-left origin) to a RECT{left=W*x, top=H*(1-y-h), right=W*(x+w), bottom=H*(1-y)} on the stack, gets the base context via Renderer::getContext (renderer+0x110) and calls vtbl[0xB4] = slot 45 with NumRects=1 (r1=#1), pRects=r2=&RECT. W,H come from the u32 pair at [[renderer+0xE4]+8/+0xC] when renderer+0xE4 != 0, otherwise from the floats at [0x015B86B0]+0x14/+0x18. Applied by gfx:Renderer::applyScissorState (0x005C2510) from the 4 floats in globals at 0x019159F8 when the scissor-enabled byte at RVA 0x0151519A is 1.
facts.arm_signature: void setScissorRect(float x /*s0*/, float y /*s1*/, float w /*s2*/, float h /*s3*/, Renderer* renderer /*r1; r0 unused*/); void STDMETHODCALLTYPE hook(ID3D11DeviceContext* ctx /*r0*/, UINT n /*r1*/, const D3D11_RECT* rects /*r2*/) (plain AAPCS)
facts.x86_to_arm_notes: ARM code uses the same game-side Y conversion (H*(1-...) with H taken from the CoreWindow-sized screen object when no RT size is present) that the x86 comment blames, so the fix is expected to remain needed; it is idempotent (only touches rects with negative/oversized coordinates) so it is safe to keep unconditionally. Hook needs only: game_context pointer (renderer+0x110, unchanged), game_window HWND, vtable slot 45 (confirmed by the game's own 'ldr r3,[r3,#0xb4]' = 45*4), VirtualProtect on the vtable page (d3d11.dll rdata, copy-on-write per process). CFG: the exe's indirect calls are plain 'blx r3' (no __guard_check_icall use: the guard-check pointer at 0xC37BF8 is referenced only by the load-config and one pool), so calling into the host function from the vtable slot is unrestricted. Only one call site exists, so no other D3D scissor path needs hooking. Whether the offset really reproduces on ARM must be checked on device (cannot be proven statically).

facts.arm_signature: all three hook functions are ordinary C functions; WINAPI/STDMETHODCALLTYPE expand to nothing on ARM
facts.x86_to_arm_notes: (1) Function pointers stored into IAT cells / vtable slots must be Thumb pointers (bit0 = 1): compiling win32craft.dll as thumbv7-windows gives that for free when you take the address of a function; original_* values loaded from the cells already carry bit0. (2) Pointer size and slot size stay 4 bytes, so VirtualProtect(slot, sizeof(*slot)) and the FlushInstructionCache calls are unchanged. (3) Argument passing: the x86 STDMETHODCALLTYPE callee-pops convention disappears; hook prototypes must keep exactly the same argument count and order as the original callee (D3DCompile 11 args, D3D11CreateDevice 10 args, RSSetScissorRects 3 args incl. this) - arguments beyond r3 arrive on the stack in the order shown in the arm_signature fields. (4) The install order in Win32Bootstrap does not change: all three D3D IAT/vtable patches are installed before the game constructs the owner/renderer (install_d3d_compile_trace and install_d3d11_device_compat) or right after the context exists (install_scissor_fix).

port_instructions: Constants for the ARM 1.2.8 host: ARM_D3D_COMPILE_IAT = 0x00C370B4; ARM_D3D11_CREATE_DEVICE_IAT = 0x00C37A50. These are the ONLY RVAs this area needs. RVA_128_DXGI_DEVICE3_IID / RVA_128_D3D_CONTEXT_IID / RVA_128_D3D_ANNOTATION_IID have no ARM use (ARM equivalents, if ever wanted: 0x00DBC2C4 / 0x00DBC3FC / 0x00DBC3DC).

Win32Bootstrap (ARM): set host_is_windows7 = FALSE (remove the GetVersion probe). Delete calls to patch_win7_dxgi_device3_query_to_base, patch_win7_device2_queries_to_base and patch_win7_discard_views; delete those three functions. No game code or .rdata byte is patched by this area on ARM.

install_d3d11_device_compat(image, 0x00C37A50): keep the IAT hook only as a thin wrapper: adjusted_flags = flags | 0x20; call original_d3d11_create_device with the other 9 arguments unchanged; keep the log line. Remove: the 0xb100 feature-level filter, the driver_type==1 -> WARP retry (the game retries with D3D_DRIVER_TYPE_WARP itself at 0x5BC3EC), the captured_base_device/captured_base_context AddRef logic, the host_is_116 blocks, and the matching 'Windows 7 fallback' / captured_* release code in initialize_game_d3d. Store the original with the Thumb bit as read from the cell.

install_d3d_compile_trace(image, 0x00C370B4): for the first ARM bring-up make win32_d3d_compile a pure forwarder with failure logging: call original_d3d_compile(source, size, name, defines, include_handler, entry, target, flags1, flags2, code, errors) with include_handler passed through UNCHANGED, and keep only the 'if (FAILED) log source/entry/target/HRESULT + errors blob text' block. Delete win32_include_open/close, win32_include, shader_include_directory and the D3D_COMPILE_STANDARD_FILE_INCLUDE branch (the ARM game always passes its own HeaderInclude object).

Include proxy (Win32IncludeProxy, win32_include_proxy_open/close) and patch_hlsl_lod_intrinsic: keep OUT of the first ARM build. They are source-compatible with the ARM game (ID3DInclude slot0 Open(this,type,file,parent,ppData,pBytes), slot1 Close(this,data); HeaderInclude at vtable 0x0136B164 ignores type/parent, Close is a no-op) so they can be re-enabled unchanged if the log shows a D3DCompile failure mentioning CalculateLevelOfDetailUnclamped; in that case the only literal to substitute is 'tex.CalculateLevelOfDetailUnclamped(TextureSampler0, uv)' (present once, in data/shaders/hlsl/util.fxh).
Delete patch_hlsl_root_signature completely: neither ROOT_SIGNATURE nor MinecraftRootSignature exists in the 1.2.8 shader sources.

install_scissor_fix(game_context): keep exactly as on x86 (slot index 45 of the context vtable; original_set_scissor_rects saved; hook = void STDMETHODCALLTYPE(ID3D11DeviceContext*, UINT, const D3D11_RECT*)). game_context must be *(ID3D11DeviceContext**)(renderer + 0x110) (unchanged offset; the game's own scissor call uses the same pointer). Install it after the game's InitDevice has run. GetClientRect(game_window) is the only other input.
Do not port install_draw_trace and its win32_draw*/win32_*_set_shader/win32_om_*/win32_clear_* stubs (dead code on 1.2.8).

Before the first shader compile make sure image+0x015B86AC holds the owner pointer and renderer+0x108 holds the owner back-pointer (set by the game's owner ctor 0x5B7E7C when the host calls the owner ctor the same way as x86 initialize_game_d3d); otherwise compileShaderProgram dereferences null while building the VERSION macro.

Exports D3D11CreateDevice/CreateDirect3D11DeviceFromDXGIDevice/CreateDXGIFactory2 of win32craft.dll (win32_host.c 15124-15181) are not referenced by the ARM 1.2.8 exe imports (it imports d3d11.dll!D3D11CreateDevice directly, nothing from dxgi.dll); keep them only if the patched ARM exe re-points imports to win32craft.dll.
open_questions: Is the CalculateLevelOfDetailUnclamped substitution really unnecessary on every target ARM device? Static evidence (same sources, same system D3DCompiler as the original UWP app, call only under VERSION >= 0xa000) says yes, but it must be confirmed by one real compile run on the ARM device (watch for 'D3DCompile failed' log lines).

Does the scissor Y offset (-599..-47 for a 688 px HWND on x86) reproduce on ARM? The game-side math (H*(1-y-h) with H from [[renderer+0xE4]+0xC] or the CoreWindow-size global 0x015B86B0+0x18) matches the x86 description but the actual runtime values depend on what the host publishes in that screen-size object (0x015B86B0, W at +0x14, H at +0x18) and in renderer+0xE4; the identity/owner of those two objects was not resolved here.
x86 RVA_128_D3D_CONTEXT_IID semantic (ID3D11DeviceContext2) is inferred from the 0.15.10 comment and the matching renderer+0x114 offset, not from x86 bytes (x86 binary unavailable).
ID3DUserDefinedAnnotation at renderer+0x140: no consumer calling BeginEvent/EndEvent was found in the renderer region; a consumer elsewhere (e.g. mce debug markers) was not exhaustively excluded.

The disk shader cache written/read around D3DCompile (path built at 0x5BE6C8-0x5BE700 via ofstream sub_3048D4) was not traced; the host's CreateFile2/path fixes (another area) must let it create files, otherwise every launch recompiles all shaders.
